# GitHub closes the idle SSH connection during the pre-push full-suite gate

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** — this is the concrete root cause behind one of the
"transient push-transport closes" that item asks us to retry. Retrying does not
help on its own: the connection is dropped with a *deterministic* trigger
(SSH idling for the duration of the suite), so every attempt fails the same way
and the agent loops, burning a full suite run each time.

## Problem

`.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full` **after** `git` has
established the SSH connection to `github.com` and **before** the ref update.
The hook produces no SSH traffic for the whole run (measured 11 min warm, 35 min
cold on this host), so the remote closes the idle connection:

```
pre-push: full-suite gate for dev/main push — running run_tests.py --scope full ...
Connection to github.com closed by remote host.
pre-push: full suite green (cached runs make repeat pushes cheap)
pre-push: mirrored gate cache entry 96dd15da... into .worklog/cache
```

The gate reports **green**, the cache entries are mirrored — and the push never
lands: `git push` exits without updating the ref and `origin/dev` is unchanged.
Observed 2026-10-31 on two consecutive attempts from
`wl-LP-0MVWIA33O004RKP7-…` in `llm-manager`; `~/.ssh/config` sets no
`ServerAliveInterval`/`TCPKeepAlive`.

Impact:

- A green full-suite run is discarded, so the most expensive part of the push is
  paid repeatedly; because each retry rebases onto a moved `dev`, the tree
  changes and the suite cache misses, so retries are *cold*.
- The output reads as success ("full suite green") while the push silently did
  not happen — the misleading signal is arguably worse than a hard failure.

## Workaround that worked (not a fix)

```bash
GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20 -o TCPKeepAlive=yes" \
  WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev
# -> d925d89d..877a6512  HEAD -> dev
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dev push whose pre-push gate runs longer than the remote's idle timeout
      succeeds, with no manual `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` override by the agent.
- [ ] Keepalives are configured in a way that survives a fresh clone/worktree
      (e.g. set by the hook or by `implement.py`'s push, not only in one
      operator's `~/.ssh/config`).
- [ ] When the ref update is still lost after a green suite, the push reports a
      distinct, loud failure (not "full suite green" followed by silence), and
      distinguishes "suite red" from "transport lost".
- [ ] A regression test covers the transport-loss path (simulated closed
      connection) and asserts the distinct failure classification.

## Notes

- `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` / `SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN` (push must run from the worktree)
  is a separate defect; both were hit in the same session. This item is only the
  transport side.
- Related: `~/.ssh/config` on the multi-agent host currently has no
  `ServerAlive*` settings at all.

# Test: gate_reason classification for pre-push and finish

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC2, AC3, AC5). Test-first slice of the
dev-push reporting work: the classifier contract, the hook output and the
finish-side report are pinned before any of them is implemented.

## Why this must come first

`.githooks/pre-push` currently runs the runner with `--json >/dev/null 2>&1`
and prints the same "ERROR: Full test suite failed" for a red suite, an
expired slot wait and a killed run — the JSON that already carries
`notice_codes` is discarded. `implement.py finish` then reports
`reason: push_failed` with no cause. The classification contract has to be
executable before either side is changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests pin the classifier: every runner `notice_code` (`slot_busy`, `suite_timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed_failure`, `command_not_found`), a structured `failures` list, a `live_repo_mutation` notice, and an unparsable/absent JSON result each map to the documented `gate_reason` code.

# Test: push transport-retry policy

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC4, AC5). Test-first slice of the
transport-retry work.

## Why this must come first

Three pushes needed a manual retry loop after a green cached gate followed by
`Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` — `git_push_to_dev()`
currently returns `False` on any non-timeout, non-non-fast-forward failure, so
the caller cannot tell "retry later" from "fix the code". The retry policy
(retryable patterns, attempt bound, backoff, same cwd, no gate bypass) must be
pinned before it is implemented so the allowlist can never silently widen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test pins the retryable patterns: `Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`, `remote end hung up unexpectedly` and `kex_exchange_identification` are retried; auth, branch-policy and other errors are not.
- [ ] A test pins the attempt bound (initial attempt plus two retries) and jittered exponential backoff, and asserts a `PushTimeoutError` is never retried.
- [ ] A test asserts every attempt uses the **same cwd** as the first attempt and the same argv/env — no `--no-verify`, no `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` or other bypass injection — so the pre-push gate runs again and serves its cached full-suite entry.
- [ ] A test asserts non-fast-forward failures keep their existing dedicated recovery (no transport retry) and that an exhausted retry trail reports the attempt count, the backoff used and the final reason.
- [ ] Stubs only (a fake `Popen`/process factory plus the hermetic git sandbox); no ad-hoc suite invocations and no real network access.
- [ ] Across the three test slices, new/updated tests cover FIFO fairness (cross-process), hook classification of slot-busy vs red suite vs timeout, finish reporting of a gate infrastructure failure, and transport-retry policy (retryable vs non-retryable stderr, attempt bound, same cwd) — tests use stubs/hermetic git sandboxes only, with no ad-hoc suite invocations.

1. New module `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` with a
   recording fake process factory driven by a scripted stderr/return-code
   sequence, and a `time.sleep` spy for the backoff.
2. Table-driven cases for retryable vs non-retryable stderr.
3. Same-cwd / same-argv / same-env assertions across attempts.
4. Leave the tests red for the implementing slice.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — new: retry policy, attempt bound, same-cwd, no-bypass assertions
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` under test

- No network access and no real long sleeps (monkeypatch the sleep).
- UK English throughout.

- Retry-policy test module, red then green with the implementing slice.

# Live-repo guard fails a run when a concurrent `wl sync` moves `refs/heads/worklog/data`

## Target outcome

A full-suite run must not be failed — and must not lose its green cache entry —
because another agent's concurrent `wl sync` moved the Worklog data ref.

**Observed** while finishing SA-0MVQQ9KZO0010XXS (2026-11-01):

```
run_tests.py --scope full → success: false
live-repo mutation detected: … moved ref refs/heads/worklog/data:
  0067d646089788ee530ff8856bd481d7bd1cd7c7 -> 96ea6f021c940ed2374e353de9f1df84f9438e6d
  (in the worktree AND in the main checkout)
```

Every test suite passed (`suites.all.returncode == 0`, 835/835 node tests, pytest
green), but the outer guard's verdict forces `success: false`, so no green
full-suite cache entry is written, and `implement.py finish`'s gate reports
"infrastructure reason" with no structured failures.

## Root cause

`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` excludes `refs/worklog/*` (`WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX`)
from the mutation surface, but the Worklog data ref also lives — and moves —
under `refs/heads/worklog/data`. Concurrent `wl sync` (sibling `implement.py
finish` pushes, the herdr downtime worker) moves it while any suite runs, so the
guard reports it as a mutation of the guarded checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Excluded as concurrency churn.** `refs/heads/worklog/data`
  (and the `refs/heads/worklog/` namespace generally) is excluded from the
  live-repo mutation surface, derived from the ref name (never a work-item
  pattern), reported instead as an informational note.
- [ ] **AC2 — Regression pinned.** A test snapshots a fixture checkout, moves
  `refs/heads/worklog/data` externally, and asserts `_detect_live_repo_mutation`
  reports no mutation (note only).
- [ ] **AC3 — Suite-caused data movement still fails.** A suite that itself
  commits to `refs/heads/worklog/data` remains a mutation (the exclusion is
  provenance independent only if the guard cannot distinguish; if it cannot,
  document the blind spot explicitly in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`).

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (`WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX`, mutation surface)
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` / `tests/test_guarded_roots.py`
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`

## Related work

- `discovered-from:SA-0MVQQ9KZO0010XXS`
- WL-0MVPE2B8E005O0OS / SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX — guarded-roots provenance work.

## Impact

Blocks any item whose finish requires a full-scope gate while other agents are
active: the green run cannot be cached, so `implement.py finish` cannot reach
its terminal status write, and audits see a cache miss.

## Goal

As the operator, I want the 2026-10-31 test-slot starvation fix proved shut with post-fix
measurements, and the remaining cross-consumer duplicate-suite vector removed, so that no agent
session loses minutes queueing for a 1–3 s test run and no two consumers pay twice for the same
full suite.

## Problem statement

The fast-lane fix (`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`, shipped `a2659c38` on 2026-10-31T23:21) delivered the
separate `test-fast` semaphore namespace, the re-derived `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 6` and
the `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane` reporting. Two gaps remain from the original RCA item
(`LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`, llm repo — closed as superseded by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`):

1. **No post-fix measurement.** Its AC5 ("median blocked time per work item falls materially below
   ~10 min/test call; evidence recorded") was never executed. A preliminary scan of the 30 pi
   session logs touched since `a2659c38` found 12 `slot_wait_seconds` samples, all `0.00 s`, and
   zero `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notices — encouraging, but too small a sample to close
   the question, and it says nothing about the two dominant wait categories (`implement finish` and
   the dev-push full-suite gate), which appear as `wait_for_job` blocks, not `run_tests.py` JSON.
2. **Verdicts are not reusable across consumers.** `run_cached()` keys on either the loose worktree
   fingerprint or — when the caller passes an explicit would-be-commit tree SHA — on
   `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. `implement.py` finish passes a tree SHA; the pre-push gate, the test
   CLI and the audit path pass nothing and therefore keep historical loose-worktree keys
   (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Explicit-fingerprint override" says so outright). A green
   full-suite verdict therefore cannot be carried between the pre-commit staged tree and the pushed
   commit, so a dev push re-executes the full suite even when an identical tree was validated
   minutes earlier.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — needs evidence, not anecdotes, that the critical starvation fix worked:
  *As the operator, I want a recorded p50/p90/max of post-fix slot wait so I can close the RCA with
  data rather than with the fix's assertion.*
- **Agent session** — *As an agent pushing to `dev`, I want the gate to reuse a green verdict for
  the tree I am pushing so my push does not cost a second 7–9 minute suite run.*

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` + `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`: two lanes
  (`test`, `test-fast`), ceilings 6 and 4, `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane`/`slot_lanes` reported,
  `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notice at ≥ 1 s.
- `skill/test_cache.py`: `compute_tree_state(index_file)` → `git write-tree` SHA;
  `run_cached(..., fingerprint=<sha>)` keys lookup and store with
  `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE`; `query_cached()` stays worktree-only by design.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: finish no longer runs a full suite at all — it defers to
  the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`) and passes the tree SHA for its changed-scope verdict
  (`SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB`).
- `.githooks/pre-push` (SorraAgents, v3): full-suite gate runs
  `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` with **no** `--fingerprint`, i.e. worktree-keyed.
  It also **ignores the pushed `local_sha`** entirely (only `remote_ref` selects the gate), so the
  suite validates whatever the checkout happens to contain — there is no pushed-commit guard in
  this hook yet (the `llm` repo's diverged v4 hook has one: `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9`).
  `.githooks/pre-push.v2` (installed into other projects) deliberately has no suite gate, so it
  needs no change. Per-repo hooks diverge: `~/projects/llm/.githooks/pre-push` is a separate v4
  variant with its own pushed-commit guard and a `--project-root` argument.

## Desired change

1. Re-measure the post-fix wait distribution and record it (with the method) in this item.
2. Give the pre-push full-suite gate a pushed-commit guard and a tree-keyed fingerprint (plumbed
   through the runner CLI), so the gate measures the tree it pushes and its verdict lands in the
   same namespace as the finish gate's, and is reused when the tree matches.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Post-fix re-measurement recorded.** A reproducible analysis (commands/script cited in the item)
   over every pi session log covering at least 24 h after `a2659c38` (or all sessions since
   2026-10-31T23:21 if fewer) reports, per wait category — (a) `run_tests.py` slot wait, (b)
   `implement finish`, (c) dev-push full-suite gate — the call count and p50/p90/max wall clock.
   Pass: no run reports `slot_wait_seconds > 120 s`, partial-run (`test-fast`) p90 < 30 s, and no
   `queued N s` notice ≥ 30 s. Any miss is recorded honestly and filed as follow-up work, not
   smoothed over.
2. **The pre-push gate keys on the pushed tree.** The gate first adds the pushed-commit guard this
   hook currently lacks (pushed `local_sha` must equal the checkout's `HEAD` and the tree must be
   clean, with a loud refusal naming the commit, the HEAD, the tree path and the recovery step —
   the `llm` v4 hook's wording is the precedent), then computes that commit's tree SHA and passes
   it explicitly, so the verdict is stored and looked up with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. When the
   guard fails or the tree SHA cannot be computed the gate refuses rather than falling back to a
   loose worktree key (fail-closed, matching the cache's provenance contract).
3. **Cross-consumer reuse proven.** A test demonstrates that a full-suite verdict recorded for tree
   *T* by one caller (finish gate / tree-keyed `run_cached`) is served as a cache hit to the
   pre-push gate for the same *T*, and that a different tree misses. The gate reports cache
   hit/miss (and the reused entry's age) in its stderr/JSON output so a served verdict is visible.
4. **Runner CLI surface + docs.** `run_tests.py` accepts an explicit tree fingerprint for
   `--scope full` (the parameter already threads through `run_suite`/`run_all`), documented in
   `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`; `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` and the hook's header comment are
   updated — the "callers that pass nothing keep worktree keys … (test-skill CLI, audit, pre-push)"
   sentence must no longer describe the pre-push gate.
5. **Tests.** Deterministic tests cover: the gate computes and passes the pushed tree SHA; a
   same-tree second run is a hit; a different tree is a miss; fail-closed when `HEAD != local_sha`,
   when the tree is dirty, or when the tree SHA is unavailable; worktree-keyed callers' cache keys
   are unchanged byte for byte. Existing cache/provenance, finish-gate-tree and pre-push hook tests
   stay green.
6. **Rollout is explicit, not implicit.** The item records that the `llm` repo's diverged v4 hook
   needs its own change (follow-up item), and that `pre-push.v2` consumers are unaffected.
7. **Testing/validation criterion.** Every new behaviour above is exercised by an automated test
   that fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Repository scope:** implementation lands in this repo only (`skill/test_cache.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `.githooks/pre-push`, docs, tests). The `llm` repo's v4 hook is
  a follow-up in that repo; `ContextHub` and others receive `pre-push.v2` (no suite gate) and need
  nothing.
- **No synthetic saturation.** Measurement must be read-only log analysis; the host is live and a
  synthetic burst would manufacture the very contention being measured (same deliberate scope
  decision as `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`).
- **Cache correctness first.** Never degrade to a state-independent fallback key and never serve a
  tree verdict for a different tree; an unfingerprintable run simply executes fresh.
- **POSIX `sh` hook.** No new dependency, no `bash`-isms in `.githooks/pre-push`.
- **Test execution policy.** All test runs go through the test skill (`run_tests.py`); no ad-hoc
  `pytest` invocations.
- **Do not edit the pacer/lane semantics** delivered by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — this item only
  measures them and changes cache keying.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` — tree-SHA helper usable from a committed (not just staged) state, plus the
  existing `fingerprint_kind` plumbing.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — CLI flag for an explicit tree fingerprint, threaded to
  `run_suite`/`run_all`/`run_cached`.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — add the pushed-commit guard, compute `HEAD^{tree}`, pass it, report hit/miss.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — same-tree hit / different-tree miss / fail-closed cases.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py` — cross-consumer reuse assertion.
- `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs` — hook-level assertions (flag presence, refusal paths).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — contract updates.
- Measurement: pi session logs under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` plus existing tooling in
  `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` as the pattern for a one-off analysis script.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — measurement window is thin.** ~13 h of post-fix logs with 12 samples today; if the
  window yields too few samples the criterion is "no regression observed in N samples", clearly
  labelled, with a re-check date. *Mitigation:* report sample counts alongside percentiles.
- **Risk — cache poisoning by a wrong tree key.** A bug here could serve a green verdict for an
  untested tree. *Mitigation:* fail closed, plus explicit same-tree/different-tree tests and reuse of
  the already-audited `fingerprint_kind` machinery.
- **Risk — hook divergence drift.** Per-repo copies (`llm` v4, `pre-push.v2`) mean the fix can land
  in `SorraAgents` yet not reach a project. *Mitigation:* AC6 + a follow-up item per diverged hook.
- **Risk — scope creep into the wider RCA amplifiers** (`drive` nested waits, finish lock
  serialisation, agents raising `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to 5400 s). Recorded as linked follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption —** the dominant residual cost is the dev-push gate suite, not finish, because finish
  no longer runs a full suite (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`). The AC1 measurement either confirms or
  refutes this, and refutation re-opens the amplifier list rather than silently narrowing the item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — fast lane + calibrated ceiling + `slot_wait` reporting (**shipped
  `a2659c38`**); supersedes AC1–AC3 of the original RCA.
- `LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM` (llm) — the original RCA item; closed as superseded, its AC4 residual and
  AC5 re-measurement are this item's scope.
- `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81` — full-suite testing deferred to the dev-push gate (makes AC4 of the old
  item largely obsolete and creates the reuse gap addressed here).
- `SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB` / `SA-0MVQHVKUH009VQMD` — tree-bound finish verdicts and their documented
  contract (the precedent this item extends to the pre-push gate).
- `SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D` — runner duration/timeout/kill/slot-wait facts (source of
  `slot_wait_seconds`).
- Open amplifiers, already tracked: `SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` (a low-ceiling waiter never probes
  higher-numbered free slots), `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI` (dev pushes starve/flake under load),
  `SA-0MVEEALZR0029DD7` (single-flight coalescing of identical in-flight suite runs).
- `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — finish gate: classify timeouts/kills and report slot queue wait separately.
- Pushed-commit-guard precedents: `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9` (llm v4 hook guard),
  `LP-0MVTI2K2A002HCGT` (llm: gate validated the main checkout, not the pushed commit — completed).
- Adjacent, open, *not* in scope: `SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3` / `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` (implement.py must
  push from the tree it is pushing) and `SA-0MVV1V1DB0035Q6B` (gate did not execute for the pushed
  commit) — they concern which tree `finish` pushes, not the hook's own fingerprint.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (producer, interactive reply):** "`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` already holds AC1–AC3; what should
  happen to `LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`?" — Options: (a) close as superseded and file the residual here,
  (b) narrow the `llm` item and implement cross-repo, (c) close as fully superseded and drop
  AC4/AC5.
  **Answer: "1. A"** — close the `llm` item as superseded; the residual (AC4 gap + AC5
  re-measurement) is filed as this item. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research:
  verified `a2659c38` in `SorraAgents` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT == 6`, `test-fast` lane,
  live `slot_lane=fast`, `slot_wait=0.00007s`); verified none of the named files exist in the `llm`
  checkout, so an `llm`-store item could not satisfy worktree isolation.
- **Q2 (producer, interactive reply):** "Residual scope?" — Options: (a) re-measure only,
  (b) re-measure + tree-keyed pre-push gate, (c) re-measure + the wider amplifiers from the RCA.
  **Answer: "2. b"**; producer also asked for follow-up work to be recommended and offered as new
  work items rather than silently folded in. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research:
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Explicit-fingerprint override" documents that the pre-push
  gate keys on loose worktree state; `run_cached`/`run_suite` already accept an explicit tree
  fingerprint, so the change is a CLI + hook plumbing problem, not a cache redesign.
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection, no producer input needed):** "Does `implement finish` still run
  a full suite whose verdict the pre-push gate could reuse?" — **Answer: no**; finish defers the
  full suite to the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`, `fe85415a`, 2026-10-19), which is why the
  old AC4 is re-scoped to cross-consumer keying rather than finish→pre-push handoff. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` step 3b comment.

### Related work items

# Intake: Remove assignee when a session finishes

## Problem statement

Whenever a skill session finishes — returning its work item to `open`, `blocked`
or `completed` — the item's `assignee` must be cleared, because a non-empty
assignee is a scheduling hold and `wl next` skips held items. Release is now the
`StatusLifecycle` default, yet held items still appear: the helper only clears a
hold **it set itself**, so a pre-existing agent claim (including the claim
AGENTS_GLOBAL step 1 tells the agent to make *before* the skill runs) survives
the skill's terminal transition, and sessions that end without reaching a
terminal step (SIGKILL, timeout, context exhaustion, closed pane) leave the claim
behind entirely.

## Users

- **Dispatcher / `wl next` consumer** — "As a dispatcher, I want every finished
  session to leave its item unheld, so finished work is dispatchable instead of
  invisible."
  - Example: a refactor session claims an item, runs, and ends; the item must not
    stay on `refactor-agent`.
- **Implementing agent** — "As an agent claiming per the workflow, I want the
  skill I invoke to release my pre-claim when it finishes, so I never inherit my
  own stale hold."
- **Producer / operator** — "As the producer, I want my deliberate `Map` hold and
  any `needsProducerReview` flag to survive every automated release, so
  scheduling intent is never wiped by a cleanup."
- **On-call maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want a bounded reaper that names
  every stale claim it releases, so an orphaned hold is fixed without source
  archaeology."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Release covers any non-producer claim on a terminal outcome.** After every
   skill terminal outcome (`open`, `blocked`, `completed`/`in_review`) the
   persisted `assignee` is empty unless it is the producer hold (`Map`) or the
   item carries `needsProducerReview` — including a claim the run did **not**
   set itself. Proven by extending the table-driven matrix
   (`tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py`) with an externally pre-claimed
   row per skill terminal entry point, read back through a real `wl` store.
2. **Session-level backstop.** A shared release helper runs on every skill's
   final step and on the abort/error/signal paths of skill scripts, so a session
   that never reaches a terminal lifecycle step still releases its claim; a
   regression test drives the helper through both the normal end-of-session path
   and an interrupting signal, asserting the persisted assignee is empty.
3. **Bounded stale-claim reaper.** A TTL-bounded scan (documented default,
   configurable) releases non-producer claims older than the TTL, records each
   release in machine-readable output and as a comment naming the previous
   assignee, and is idempotent — producer holds, `needsProducerReview` items and
   `completed`/`deleted` items are never touched. Tests cover release, idempotent
   re-run, and producer-hold preservation. Success metric: after one reaper
   pass (or one sync cycle where it is hooked), a store scan finds zero
   non-producer claims older than the TTL on non-terminal items.
4. **Existing dispatch-blocking holds cleared.** The three currently held,
   non-terminal items are released and verifiably dispatchable again:
   `SA-0MVWEH5ZA000ZIEW` (`refactor-agent`, `open`/`intake_complete`),
   `SA-0MUUIGDKC004UJL0` (`Agent`, `blocked`/`idea`),
   `SA-0MM8W6OK5061NLKG` (`opencode`, `open`/`done`). Historical `completed`/`done`
   non-`Map` holds stay untouched (not dispatch-blocking) and that exclusion is
   documented.
5. **Tests and docs.** New and changed behaviour is covered by tests that fail
   before the change; the assignee-release invariant text, the implement-skill
   reference and the worklog-sync docs reflect the widened rule and the reaper;
   "All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries."
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer holds are sacrosanct.** `Map` (the producer assignee) and any item
  with `needsProducerReview` must survive every release path — this is the one
  documented exception to the widened rule.
- **No cross-repo changes.** herdr (hydrator, downtime dispatcher) and ContextHub
  (`wl`, `src/claim-hold.ts`, `syncClaimHoldTtlHours`) are separate repositories;
  this item's guarantee must be deliverable from `skill/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`
  and `tests/` in this repo, and may *reuse* their mechanisms (for example the
  sync claim-hold TTL) but must not require a change there.
- **Ownership rule is identity-agnostic but producer-aware:** a finishing run may
  clear **any** non-producer assignee on a terminal transition (operator decision
  Q2 = C), not only its own.
- **No backlog rewrites.** Only the three named non-terminal holds are cleared;
  historical terminal holds stay as they are.
- **Ordering.** The release stays the run's **last** lifecycle action — it must
  not move ahead of post-push verification, worktree cleanup or the completion
  comment (SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H).
- **Concurrency safety.** A release must never clear a claim held by a live
  session of a *different* skill (audit racing implement is the known failure
  mode, SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H); the reaper's TTL and the "actively worked ⇒
  `in_progress`" invariant provide the guard, and the terminal-transition release
  only fires on the transition itself.
- Build → test → commit ordering, no ad-hoc test invocations (route through the
  test skill), and the dev-push full-suite gate apply as usual.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`: `StatusLifecycle` releases the assignee on
  **every** exit path by default, but `_should_release_assignee()` returns
  `False` when the context manager was constructed without `assignee=` — so a
  hold it never established is never cleared. `preserve_assignee_on_exit=True` is
  the documented opt-out; `clear_assignee_on_exit` is deprecated and inert.
- Explicit `assignee=""` writes on terminal branches: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  (all failure resets, signal/safety-reset, timeout `_release_orphaned_child_claim`,
  drive finalise), `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` (`finish`, `auto-complete`,
  `abort`, failure resets), `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (every terminal
  verdict).
- `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py`: table-driven matrix plus an AST
  discovery guard over `skill/*/scripts/*.py` for assignee mutation; pinned
  intentional holds (producer `Map`, `needsProducerReview`, agent-log-review
  creation, `verify_context_reduction` restore).
- Documented residual window: SIGKILL with no surviving supervisor
  (`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` § Assignee release…), backstopped only
  by `wl sync`'s `syncClaimHoldTtlHours` (24 h, ContextHub) and the herdr
  hydrator, which itself misses pane-less driven children (SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR).
- Skills that transition without claiming — `plan` (`ensure_claimed`, no
  assignee), `find-related` / `refactor` (`StatusLifecycle(..., restore_on_exit=True)`)
  — cannot release a claim made outside the script.
- Live store evidence (non-deleted, non-`Map` claims): `SA-0MVWEH5ZA000ZIEW`
  (`refactor-agent`, held since 2026-10-31, session ended), `SA-0MUUIGDKC004UJL0`
  (`Agent`, blocked), `SA-0MM8W6OK5061NLKG` (`opencode`, open/done); plus ~100
  historical `completed`/`done` non-`Map` holds from before release-by-default.

## Desired change

1. **Widen the release rule in the shared helper.** `StatusLifecycle` clears any
   non-producer assignee on every exit path (success, rollback,
   `restore_on_exit`), recognising the producer identity (`Map`, configurable) and
   leaving `needsProducerReview` items alone; `preserve_assignee_on_exit=True`
   stays the explicit producer-hold opt-out.
2. **Session-end backstop.** A shared release helper (candidate location
   `skill/shared/`, exposed as a skill/CLI entry point) invoked from each skill's
   final report step and from the abort/error/signal handlers of skill scripts, so
   "session finished" — not only "script reached its terminal branch" — releases
   the claim.
3. **Stale-claim reaper.** A TTL-bounded, idempotent, producer-aware scan that
   releases orphaned claims, with reported output (item, previous assignee, age)
   and a comment per release; runnable from the existing sync/cleanup paths
   without changes in herdr or ContextHub.
4. **One-off cleanup** of the three named holds plus a read-back proving they are
   dispatchable.
5. **Docs**: canonical invariant wording (AGENTS_GLOBAL), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
   `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, plus the ownership/identity rule and reaper
   semantics in a dedicated reference section.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — widen `_should_release_assignee`/release
  paths; producer-identity recognition; keep `preserve_assignee_on_exit`
- `skill/shared/claim_release.py` (new) — session-end release helper + reaper
  scan, TTL config, reporting
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — hook the reaper into the post-sync path
  (in-tree side only)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py`,
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — terminal branches call the shared
  release; signal/abort handlers extended
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`, `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py`,
  `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — release an externally-set claim when the
  run finishes
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — natural end-of-session anchor for the
  release helper
- `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` — new externally-pre-claimed rows
  and reaper/producer-preservation cases
- `tests/test_assignee_release_docs.py` — invariant/documentation assertions
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` (new, if the
  reference material outgrows the existing sections)

## Related work

- **SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH** — Enforce assignee release on every terminal outcome
  across all skills (completed: made release the default in `StatusLifecycle`;
  this item closes the "hold the helper never set" and "no terminal step
  reached" gaps it left).
- **SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM** — implement/intake: clear assignee on completion
  regardless of outcome (completed; per-skill groundwork).
- **SA-0MVVF6GWG005VIFK** — T1: table-driven assignee-release regression matrix
  (completed; the enforcement point this item extends).
- **SA-0MVVF6Y38004T5OZ** — Migrate callers and pin intentional holds
  (completed; `preserve_assignee_on_exit` semantics).
- **SA-0MVVF75ZA007XNKB** — Release assignee on signal, timeout and drive paths
  (completed; implement.py kill-path releases; documents the SIGKILL residual
  window this item reaper-closes).
- **SA-0MVVF7CZ6002UDKU** — Document the assignee-release invariant (completed).
- **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** — Only mark as complete when fully complete (open;
  finalisation ordering — the release must remain the *last* lifecycle action, so
  this item must not move the release earlier).
- **SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR** — Driven child sessions do not hold the per-child lock,
  so the herdr hydrator demotes them mid-implementation (open; the hydrator is a
  backstop this item's reaper complements).
- **SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E** — TTL-bounded monotonic claim-hold guard (completed;
  precedent for TTL semantics).
- **SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ** — `wl sync --if-idle` reverts actively-worked items
  (completed; `syncClaimHoldTtlHours` claim-hold machinery the reaper can reuse).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: releasing a live sibling's claim.** A terminal transition that clears
  *any* non-producer assignee could wipe a concurrent live claim (audit racing
  implement, SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H). Mitigation: only fire on the transition the run
  itself performs, keep the TTL for the reaper, and keep the
  "actively worked ⇒ `in_progress`" invariant asserted by tests.
- **Risk: producer-hold regression.** Widening the rule could clear `Map` or a
  `needsProducerReview` hold. Mitigation: pinned rows in the matrix plus explicit
  tests for both, and the reaper's producer-aware predicate sharing one helper.
- **Risk: reaper flapping on long legit runs.** A genuinely long session exceeding
  the TTL would be released. Mitigation: reaper uses the claim's
  `updatedAt`/`activityAt` (refreshed by any mutation), default TTL documented,
  and every release is commented on the item so it is recoverable.
- **Risk: scope creep.** A store-wide "no stale claims ever" linter, herdr-side
  changes and cross-repo `wl` work are tempting; they are recorded as linked
  opportunities, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the producer identity is `Map` (per AGENTS_GLOBAL) with at most
  a configurable override; no project uses a different producer name.
- **Assumption:** reuse of ContextHub's `syncClaimHoldTtlHours` semantics is
  acceptable without modifying that repository; if a change there is genuinely
  required it becomes a separate linked item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which termination paths must release the assignee? (A) skill-script
  terminal paths only, (B) A + clear an externally pre-set agent claim the run
  observed, (C) B + a session-level backstop for abandoned sessions."
  — Answer (operator, interactive): **C**, "with the one exception that a
  'producer' claim should be left intact". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Ownership rule: whose claim may a run clear? (A) only its own self-set
  hold, (B) its own hold plus a hold matching the run's own agent identity,
  (C) any non-producer assignee (never `Map`, never a `needsProducerReview`
  hold) on a terminal transition." — Answer (operator, interactive): **C**.
  Source: interactive reply. Consistent with the Q1 producer exception.
- Q3: "Existing stale holds / historical backlog? (A) in scope — clear the 3
  currently dispatch-blocking holds, (B) separate `chore` item, (C) out of
  scope." — Answer (operator, interactive): **A**. Source: interactive reply.
  Research: the three holds were identified by reading the local worklog store
  read-only (non-deleted items with a non-`Map` assignee on a non-terminal
  state); ~100 `completed`/`done` non-`Map` holds were found and are excluded as
  not dispatch-blocking.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MV9DUE6F006SK1H** – Ship release gate re-homed onto the producer assignee hold (from WL-0MV85WESL002SD0F) (completed)
- **SA-0MVA79DNT001HQBB** – AGENTS_GLOBAL.md claim pattern: status-neutral assignee CAS + assignee-hold convention (from WL-0MV85WH2K0010ISF) (completed)
- **SA-0MVXUSED6008J04R** – Decide finalisation ordering design and contract (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvvf6y38004t5oz, abort, acceptable, acceptance, action (+380 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvvf6y38004t5oz, 0mvvf75za007xnkb, abandoned, abort, acceptable (+373 more)

## Goal (user story)

*As a framework maintainer*, I need the semaphore's slot-**discovery** rule pinned
by unit tests, so a future semaphore change cannot silently reintroduce the
snapshot-ceiling starvation that stalled a test run for 105 minutes
(SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

`Semaphore._try_acquire_slot()` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` iterates
`range(self.max_workers)` and `flock`s the first free file. `max_workers` is
resolved once in `__init__`, so a waiter created with `max_workers=2` **never
opens slot files `2..7`**, even when they exist in the namespace and are
unlocked. Live evidence (2026-10-31): `/run/user/1000/pi-semaphores/test/` held
slot files `0`-`7`, slots `2,3,4,6,7` were free, and the waiter owned no lock.

This child adds the **failing-first** unit tests only. The implementation is
child "Semaphore: dynamic slot discovery across the namespace", which removes
the strict `xfail` markers added here.

## Scope (tests only)

File: `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` (hermetic — the existing
`_isolate_lock_dir` autouse fixture already points `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` at
`tmp_path`):

- **Discovery:** a waiter constructed with `max_workers=2` against a namespace
  whose slots `0` and `1` are both held, which has already polled at least
  twice, must acquire within the documented bound (one poll interval plus one
  `flock` attempt) once slot files `2..7` are created and left free.
- **Poll cadence:** the documented maximum poll interval is `1.5 x
  _RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS` = 75 ms with jitter enabled and 50 ms with jitter off;
  pin that no attempt sleeps longer than that cap and that a long-waiting
  consumer performs many attempts (`> 3`), not one.
- **Own-ceiling floor:** a waiter never creates slot files beyond its own
  `max_workers` (only `0..1`), even when higher-index slots exist.
- **Late slot observed across many cycles:** create the new slot only after at
  least three poll cycles and assert the waiter still acquires it.

## Constraints

- Tests are hermetic: temporary `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, no host-wide pool, no
  reliance on `/run/user`.
- Behaviour that does not exist yet is pinned with
  `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0 discovery not implemented; marker removed by the implementation child")`
  — repo precedent: `_GATE_XFAIL` in
  `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_gate_failure_reason.py`. The suite must
  stay green.
- No ad-hoc suite invocations — every run goes through `/skill:test`.

## Repo note

The affected code is this repository's framework source, consumed by other
projects via `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink. Run
`implement.py start SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` **from this checkout** so the worktree is
a SorraAgents worktree and `wl` resolves the `SA-*` item against this store.


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — new unit regressions.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — read-only reference (`_try_acquire_slot`, `_ensure_slots`, `_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS`, `_jittered_retry_delay`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** A unit test starts a `max_workers=2` waiter against a namespace whose slots `0` and `1` are held, lets it poll at least twice, then creates slot files `2..7` free; the waiter acquires one of the new slots well inside its timeout. Marked `xfail(strict=True)` while the fix is absent.
- **AC2** A test pins the maximum poll interval (50 ms base, `[0.5, 1.5]x` jittered, so 75 ms maximum) and asserts a long waiter makes many attempts (`> 3`).
- **AC3** A test asserts a waiter creates no slot files beyond its own `max_workers`.
- **AC4** A test creates the new slot only after at least three poll cycles and asserts the waiter still observes and acquires it.
- **AC5** The new behaviour assertions carry strict `xfail` markers naming this work item; the suite is green (`/skill:test`, changed scope) with the markers in place.
- **AC6** All tests are hermetic (temporary `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, no host-wide pool) and use no ad-hoc suite invocation.

> The block below restates the parent criteria this child satisfies (parent item
> SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0). It is the machine-checkable coverage mapping, not additional
> child criteria.

### Acceptance Criteria — parent coverage (restated)

- **Parent AC1** — Bounded acquisition once any slot in the namespace is free: a waiter that began polling when only slots 0..N-1 existed must acquire within a documented bound (one poll interval plus one flock attempt) as soon as any slot file in its namespace is free, including slot files created by a later, higher-ceiling process; a max_workers=2 waiter acquires one of the new slots created after it began polling, well inside its timeout.
- **Parent AC2** — Documented maximum poll interval, no unbounded backoff: the poll cadence has a documented maximum interval (50 ms base, jittered 0.5-1.5x when jitter is enabled) and a test pins that a long-waiting consumer still observes slots created after it began waiting (many poll cycles, not one); no backoff may grow without a documented cap.
- **Parent AC4** — Testing/validation: new and updated tests cover AC1 (slot created after the waiter started), AC2 (max interval pinned; late-created slot observed) and AC3 (genuine saturation notice); tests are hermetic (temporary PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR, no host-wide pool) and use real subprocesses where the behaviour is cross-process, with no ad-hoc suite invocations.

## Goal (user story)

*As a producer/release operator*, I need proof that a `slot_busy` verdict means
the pool really was full for the whole wait, and *as a framework maintainer* I
need the cross-process discovery rule pinned, so "the waiter is stuck" can never
be mistaken for "retry later" (SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

# Test runs exhaust /tmp inodes under multi-agent load — disk-backed TMPDIR + stale pytest-root prune

## Goal (user story)

As an agent or operator running the test suite / dev-push gate, I want test and
build subprocesses to use disk-backed temporary storage and stale test temp
roots to be pruned automatically, so a host with many concurrent agents cannot
exhaust `/tmp` inodes and turn a green change into a blocked push.

## Problem statement

During **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** (tce-main-street) the dev-push gate failed its
full-suite run with an `ENOSPC` raised inside
`PlaywrightBrowserProvider.createContext`, reported by the gate as an
`unparsed`/infrastructure failure. Diagnosis:

- `/tmp` is **tmpfs with 1,048,576 inodes**; it was **100 % used** (`df -i /tmp`
  → `IUse% 100`, `IFree 0`) while the byte budget was only ~24 % used.
- The inode pressure came from many small files: stale
  `/tmp/pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-*` roots (~5–20k files each; 42 stale roots
  ≈ 312k files), Playwright/Chromium profiles, and `tsx`/node compile caches.
- `systemd-tmpfiles` only carries `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d` — age-based, so
  rapid multi-agent churn exhausts inodes long before the 10-day sweep.
- Nothing overrides `TMPDIR`, so every suite/build subprocess defaults to the
  small tmpfs. Manually deleting stale pytest roots (`mtime > 20 min`) freed
  ~679k inodes and the push then passed — confirming the cause.

The gate correctly refused to push, but the failure is host-infrastructure, not
a code failure, and it blocks otherwise-green work. This is a framework/test-
tooling defect, not a tce-main-street defect.

## Desired change (option 1 + option 2)

1. **Disk-backed TMPDIR (option 1).** When the test runner spawns suite
   commands, give them a `TMPDIR` on a disk-backed filesystem (plenty of
   inodes) instead of the ambient small tmpfs. Resolve a candidate in a
   documented precedence order (explicit env override → a configured
   disk-backed dir such as `/var/tmp/pi-test-<uid>` → `tempfile.gettempdir()`),
   create it if needed, and fall back safely when no candidate is usable
   (macOS/Windows/CI).
2. **Stale test-root prune (option 2).** Before running (at least the full
   suite), prune stale `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*` roots older than a
   configurable threshold (default ~60 min), keeping the `pytest-current`
   symlink target and the N most recent roots, never touching another user's
   directories, and best-effort skipping roots that an active `pytest` process
   may hold.

Both must be **fail-open**: a prune or TMPDIR error is logged and the test run
proceeds unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Disk-backed TMPDIR for suite subprocesses.** `run_tests.py` passes a
   disk-backed `TMPDIR` to every suite command it spawns, using the documented
   precedence order and creating the directory when absent. A unit test asserts
   the env handed to the spawned command (and the fallback path when no
   disk-backed candidate exists).
2. **Stale-root prune is correct and safe.** The prune removes
   `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*` roots older than the threshold, keeps the
   `pytest-current` target and the newest roots, is scoped to the current user,
   and is a no-op when the base directory is absent. A unit test exercises it
   against a temporary fixture directory (stale root removed, current/newest
   root kept).
3. **Fail-open.** A TMPDIR- or prune-related error never changes a run's exit
   status, cache entry, or scope resolution; it is logged only. Covered by a
   test that forces the failure path.
4. **`implement.py` parity.** The `finish` build/test/push subprocesses (and
   therefore the pre-push full-suite gate) inherit the same disk-backed
   `TMPDIR`, so the observed failure mode is closed end-to-end.
5. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/testing.md` (and/or the test-skill reference)
   documents the TMPDIR precedence, the prune behaviour, and the failure
   signature: `ENOSPC` inside Playwright `createContext`, `df -i /tmp` at
   100 %, gate `reason: unparsed`/`infrastructure` — with the operator remedy.
6. **Regression pin.** A test pins the inode-exhaustion signature so the gate
   classifies it as infrastructure (never a code `test_failure`) and pins the
   TMPDIR/prune helpers.
7. **No behaviour change to test selection or caching.** Changed/full scope
   resolution, cache keys and the audit-accepted full-suite cache entry are
   unchanged.

## Key files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — TMPDIR resolution + prune hook + logging.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — propagate TMPDIR to build/test/push.
- `.githooks/pre-push`, `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — full-suite gate invocation
  (inherit the runner's TMPDIR; verify no separate temp use).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — hook install path (verify no change needed).
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — precedence, prune, failure signature, remedy.
- New tests, e.g. `tests/test_run_tests_tmpdir.py`,
  `tests/test_prune_stale_test_roots.py`.

## Related work

- Observed during **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** (tce-main-street) dev-push gate.
- Follow-up host-hardening item (option 3): age-based `systemd-tmpfiles`
  cleanup — cross-referenced, created separately.

## Risks & assumptions

- Disk-backed temp is slower than tmpfs; acceptable for test churn (correctness
  over microbenchmark). Default only when the ambient tmpfs is small.
- `/var/tmp` may not exist (macOS/Windows) → safe fallback required.
- The prune must never delete an active run's root: keep the current target and
  newest roots, use a generous age threshold, and treat errors as fail-open.
- Scope is the framework (SorraAgents), not tce-main-street.

## Evidence

- `df -i /tmp` → `1048576 1048576 0 100%`; `/` (disk) → ~30M free inodes.
- 42 stale `pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-*` roots ≈ 312k files; pruning roots
  older than 20 min freed ~679k inodes.
- Gate failure text: `ENOSPC` in `@vitest/browser` `PlaywrightBrowserProvider.createContext`;
  `notice_codes: ["unparsed_failure"]`.

# Harden /tmp inode headroom — age-based cleanup for test churn directories (host runbook)

## Goal (user story)

As the host owner of a multi-agent workstation, I want age-based cleanup of the
directories that test and build runs churn in `/tmp`, so inode headroom is
reclaimed automatically and a future runner that skips the framework prune
still cannot exhaust `/tmp` inodes.

## Context

Follow-up to the critical framework item (disk-backed `TMPDIR` + stale
pytest-root prune in `run_tests.py`/`implement.py`). That fix prevents new
inode pressure from the test runner; this item is the **host-level belt-and-
braces**: `systemd-tmpfiles` currently only carries `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d`,
so rapid multi-agent churn (stale `pytest-of-*` roots, Playwright/Chromium
profiles, `tsx`/node compile caches) can still fill the tmpfs inode table long
before the 10-day sweep. Observed in practice: `/tmp` at 100 % inodes
(1,048,576 total) while byte usage was ~24 %.

## Desired change (option 3)

Add age-based cleanup rules (systemd-tmpfiles preferred; cron acceptable where
tmpfiles is unavailable) for the high-churn temp directories, with an age
threshold longer than the longest test run, and document a runbook so the
remediation is repeatable.

Candidate patterns (refine during implementation):

- `/tmp/pytest-of-%u/pytest-*`
- `/tmp/playwright*`, `/tmp/.org.chromium.Chromium.*`, `/tmp/.com.google.Chrome.*`
- `/tmp/tsx-*`, `/tmp/node-compile-cache*`

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Rules installed and version-controlled/documented.** Age-based cleanup
   rules exist for the churn patterns above (e.g. `/etc/tmpfiles.d/pi-test-tmp.conf`
   with `e`/`q` lines, age ≥ 1 day), with the exact content recorded in the
   repo (runbook or a committed template under `docs/dev/` or `scripts/`).
2. **Verified.** `systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run` (or the cron equivalent)
   lists the intended removals, and a before/after `df -i /tmp` demonstrates
   reclaimed inodes. Evidence captured in a work-item comment.
3. **Safety.** The age threshold is strictly greater than the longest full-suite
   run (currently ~48 min measured worst case), rules are user-scoped where
   possible, and the active `pytest-current` target / newest root is never
   removed.
4. **Runbook.** `docs/dev/testing.md` (or a new `docs/dev/host-hygiene.md`)
   documents install, verify, rollback, and the inode-exhaustion failure
   signature (`ENOSPC` in Playwright `createContext`, `df -i /tmp` at 100 %,
   gate `reason: unparsed`/`infrastructure`).
5. **No repo code change required for the cleanup itself** beyond the committed
   rule template/runbook; if a scripted installer is added, it is idempotent
   and requires explicit root/host opt-in.

## Key files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/testing.md` or `docs/dev/host-hygiene.md` — runbook + rule template.
- Optional: a committed `scripts/` template for `/etc/tmpfiles.d/` (documented,
  not auto-installed without opt-in).

## Constraints

- **Requires host/root access** (`/etc/tmpfiles.d/`, `systemd-tmpfiles`). The
  repository change is documentation/template only; the host change is applied
  by the operator and evidenced in a work-item comment.
- Do **not** add rules that delete recent or active test roots.
- Complements, and does not replace, the framework TMPDIR + prune item.

## Related work

- Critical framework fix (option 1 + 2): disk-backed `TMPDIR` + stale
  pytest-root prune in `run_tests.py`/`implement.py`.
- Observed during **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** (tce-main-street) dev-push gate.

## Risks

- Over-aggressive age thresholds can delete a long-running test's temp files —
  mitigate with a threshold well above the measured worst case and user scoping.
- Host config drift between machines — the committed rule template keeps it
  reproducible.
